about: Scripted Claude Code sessions in project/ for scripts/eval-tagger.py. Each scenario's last turn is judged. 'expect' gives the right words for that turn: a list of acceptable values, null meaning the key should be left out; for the 'missing' list key, '~a|b' means not 'none' and naming at least one of a, b. A key not in 'expect' isn't scored. 'skill': 'auto' is worked out from the session: helped or unneeded when a skill ran, else none, would-help or left out. Scenarios with "set": "holdout" were written after the judge's instructions were tuned on the rest, and never used to tune them: they show how the tuning holds up on work it hasn't seen. Scenarios with "source": "hand" have a session written by hand, in the format the recorded ones are trimmed to (plus what the trimmer drops and the excerpt reads: the plan text, the feedback typed into a plan dialog, a tool result's note and a background start's status): 'record' skips them and says so, so they are never overwritten, and no tag of Claude's is scored for them, as none was asked for. "entrypoint": "claude-desktop" marks a session whose lines carry that entrypoint. A hand-written scenario's own 'about' says what its session covers.
